defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story840.Criterion7193Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 840 — See an audit trail of schedule and record changes
  Criterion 7193 — Office staff reschedules a job and it is logged: an
  audit entry records who moved the job, the old and new times, and
  the timestamp of the change.

  Assumes `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.JobFormComponent` (per the
  project's architecture spec, opened from the board at `/schedule`)
  exposes a `[data-test='job-<id>-edit-button']` trigger and a
  `[data-test='job-form']` submitted via `render_submit` with
  `scheduled_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` fields. Assumes
  `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` (`/audit`) renders a
  `[data-test='audit-entries']` list where each entry shows its actor,
  action, one `"<Field label>: <old> → <new>"` line per changed field,
  and today's date as its timestamp.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "office staff reschedules a job and it is logged" do
    scenario "moving a job from Tuesday 9:00 to Wednesday 1:00 pm is recorded" do
      given_ "office staffer Dana is logged in with an active account", context do
        user =
          Fixtures.user_fixture(%{
            email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a job is scheduled for Tuesday at 9:00 am", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Tuesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: tuesday(),
            start_time: ~T[09:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[11:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "Dana moves the job to Wednesday at 1:00 pm", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-edit-button']")
        |> render_click()

        board_live
        |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
          job: %{
            scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(wednesday()),
            start_time: "13:00",
            end_time: "15:00"
          }
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :board_live, board_live)}
      end

      then_ "an audit entry names Dana as the one who rescheduled the job", context do
        {:ok, _audit_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        assert html =~ context.user.email
        assert html =~ "rescheduled"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the audit entry records the old and new times and the timestamp of the change",
            context do
        {:ok, _audit_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/audit")

        assert html =~
                 "Scheduled date: #{Date.to_iso8601(tuesday())} → #{Date.to_iso8601(wednesday())}"

        assert html =~ "Start time: 09:00:00 → 13:00:00"
        assert html =~ Date.to_iso8601(Date.utc_today())

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp tuesday do
    monday = week_monday()
    Date.add(monday, 1)
  end

  defp wednesday do
    monday = week_monday()
    Date.add(monday, 2)
  end

  defp week_monday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
  end
end

      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Repo.Migrations.CreateAuditEntriesTable do
  use Ecto.Migration

  def change do
    create table(:audit_entries, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :actor_id, references(:users, on_delete: :nilify_all)
      add :system, :boolean, null: false, default: false
      add :action, :string, null: false
      add :subject_type, :string, null: false
      add :subject_id, :binary_id, null: false
      add :old_value, :map, null: false, default: %{}
      add :new_value, :map, null: false, default: %{}

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec, updated_at: false)
    end

    create index(:audit_entries, [:account_id])
    create index(:audit_entries, [:subject_type, :subject_id])

    # Defense in depth: audit entries are append-only. Application code
    # never exposes update/delete; these rules block it even if it did.
    execute(
      "CREATE RULE audit_entries_no_update AS ON UPDATE TO audit_entries DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS audit_entries_no_update ON audit_entries"
    )

    execute(
      "CREATE RULE audit_entries_no_delete AS ON DELETE TO audit_entries DO INSTEAD NOTHING",
      "DROP RULE IF EXISTS audit_entries_no_delete ON audit_entries"
    )
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
16	    AvailabilityBlock,
17	    ConflictDetector,
18	    Job,
19	    Recurrence,
20	    RecurringPlan
21	  }
22	
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
25	
26	  ## Jobs
27	
28	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
29	    Job
30	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
31	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
32	    |> Repo.get!(id)
33	  end
34	
35	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
36	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
37	  end
38	
39	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
40	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
41	    with {:ok, job} <-
42	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
43	           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
44	           |> Repo.insert() do
45	      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
46	        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
47	        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
48	      })
49	
50	      {:ok, job}
51	    end
52	  end
53	
54	  @doc """
55	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
56	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
57	  """
58	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
59	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
60	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
61	
62	    Job
63	    |> where(
64	      [j],
65	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
66	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
67	    )
68	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
69	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
70	    |> Repo.all()
71	  end
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
75	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
76	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
77	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
78	  """
79	  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
80	    Job
81	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
82	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
83	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
84	    |> Repo.all()
85	  end
86	
87	  @doc """
88	  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
89	  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
90	  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
91	  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
92	  """
93	  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
94	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
95	    with :ok <-
96	           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
97	             scope,
98	             cleaner_id,
99	             job.scheduled_date,
100	             job.start_time,
101	             job.end_time,

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder do
  @moduledoc """
  API other contexts call to append audit trail entries.

  Callers pass the acting scope, an action string, the subject being
  changed, and old/new value maps. Nothing here ever updates or deletes
  a row — this module only ever inserts.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Records an audit entry attributed to the scope's current user.
  """
  def record(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        action,
        subject_type,
        subject_id,
        old_value \\ %{},
        new_value \\ %{}
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(action) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    %AuditEntry{}
    |> AuditEntry.changeset(%{
      account_id: account_id,
      actor_id: scope.user && scope.user.id,
      system: false,
      action: action,
      subject_type: subject_type,
      subject_id: subject_id,
      old_value: old_value,
      new_value: new_value
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries for a subject, most recent first.
  """
  def list_for_subject(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, subject_type, subject_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(subject_type) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where(
      [e],
      e.account_id == ^account_id and e.subject_type == ^subject_type and
        e.subject_id == ^subject_id
    )
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end
end

2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Story 840: owners want to see who changed what and when (a direct MaidCentral user wish), including attributing automated recurring-job generation to the system. Entries must be immutable (criterion 7198) and filterable.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **Project-local `audit_entries` table + `Audit.Recorder`** — explicit, scoped to the events that matter, easy to attribute system actors.
12	- **paper_trail / ex_audit** — generic row-versioning; captures noise, awkward system-actor attribution, and both are lightly maintained.
13	- **Postgres triggers** — invisible to application code and hard to attribute to the acting user.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Write a project-local `CleanerCrm.Audit` context: an append-only `audit_entries` table (actor_id nullable + `system` flag, action, subject type/id, old/new value maps as JSONB, company-scoped) with a `Recorder` API called explicitly from mutating context functions. No update/delete functions are exposed; a DB rule/constraint blocks UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- Explicit call sites mean a mutation can forget to record; Credo local check or code review must watch for this in mutating context functions.
22	- JSONB old/new maps keep the schema stable as audited entities evolve.
23	- Retention/archival policy deferred until data volume warrants it.

# Audit Trail — project-local append-only audit table

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 840: owners want to see who changed what and when (a direct MaidCentral user wish), including attributing automated recurring-job generation to the system. Entries must be immutable (criterion 7198) and filterable.

## Options Considered

- **Project-local `audit_entries` table + `Audit.Recorder`** — explicit, scoped to the events that matter, easy to attribute system actors.
- **paper_trail / ex_audit** — generic row-versioning; captures noise, awkward system-actor attribution, and both are lightly maintained.
- **Postgres triggers** — invisible to application code and hard to attribute to the acting user.

## Decision

Write a project-local `CleanerCrm.Audit` context: an append-only `audit_entries` table (actor_id nullable + `system` flag, action, subject type/id, old/new value maps as JSONB, company-scoped) with a `Recorder` API called explicitly from mutating context functions. No update/delete functions are exposed; a DB rule/constraint blocks UPDATE/DELETE as defense in depth.

## Consequences

- Explicit call sites mean a mutation can forget to record; Credo local check or code review must watch for this in mutating context functions.
- JSONB old/new maps keep the schema stable as audited entities evolve.
- Retention/archival policy deferred until data volume warrants it.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence do
  @moduledoc """
  Generates the dates for a plan's series from its cadence.

  Project-local, calendar-date arithmetic (see the recurrence ADR) —
  no RRULE library, no virtual occurrences. `:weekly` steps 7 days,
  `:biweekly` 14, `:monthly` 28 (a fixed 4-week cadence, not a calendar
  month, so the weekday never drifts).

  TODO: the recurrence ADR calls for materializing against each
  account's IANA timezone (via `tzdata`) so visits stay pinned to local
  wall-clock across DST, plus a rolling 12-week horizon extended by a
  daily Oban job. Neither is implemented yet — dates here are naive
  and every plan is materialized in full up front, bounded only by its
  own `occurrence_count`.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan

  @step_days %{weekly: 7, biweekly: 14, monthly: 28}

  @doc """
  Returns a list of `%{index:, date:}` maps, one per occurrence, in
  series order starting at 1. `nil` if the plan is missing any of the
  fields a series needs.
  """
  def occurrences(%RecurringPlan{
        recurrence: recurrence,
        start_date: %Date{} = start_date,
        occurrence_count: count
      })
      when recurrence in [:weekly, :biweekly, :monthly] and is_integer(count) and count > 0 do
    step = Map.fetch!(@step_days, recurrence)

    for index <- 1..count do
      %{index: index, date: Date.add(start_date, (index - 1) * step)}
    end
  end

  def occurrences(_incomplete_plan), do: []

  @doc """
  Job attribute maps ready for `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job/2`, one
  per occurrence.
  """
  def job_attrs(%RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    Enum.map(occurrences(plan), fn %{date: date} ->
      %{
        property_id: plan.property_id,
        cleaner_id: plan.cleaner_id,
        recurring_plan_id: plan.id,
        scheduled_date: date,
        start_time: plan.start_time,
        end_time: plan.end_time
      }
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do

    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Authorization do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def authorize(action, %Scope{} = scope, resource) do
    case {action, resource} do
      {:read_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)

      {:manage_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:manage_members, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:delete_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->

defmodule CleanerCrm.Audit do
  @moduledoc """
  Read-side of the append-only audit trail: filtered listing of the
  entries `CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder` appends.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.AuditEntry
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  @doc """
  Lists the account's audit entries, most recent first, optionally
  narrowed by a filter map (string or atom keys):

  - `:subject_id` — exact match against the subject the entry is about
  - `:date_from` — inclusive lower bound (a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string)
  - `:date_to` — inclusive upper bound (a `Date` or an ISO 8601 string)

  A blank or absent value for any key leaves that filter off.
  """
  def list_entries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, filters \\ %{})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    AuditEntry
    |> where([e], e.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> filter_by_subject(fetch(filters, :subject_id))
    |> filter_by_date_from(fetch(filters, :date_from))
    |> filter_by_date_to(fetch(filters, :date_to))
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp fetch(filters, key), do: Map.get(filters, key) || Map.get(filters, to_string(key))

  defp filter_by_subject(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_subject(query, subject_id),
    do: where(query, [e], e.subject_id == ^subject_id)

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at >= ^start_of_day(date))

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),
    do: filter_by_date_from(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at < ^start_of_day(Date.add(date, 1)))

  defp filter_by_date_to(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),
    do: filter_by_date_to(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

  defp start_of_day(date), do: DateTime.new!(date, ~T[00:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
end

    |> filter_by_date_to(fetch(filters, :date_to))
    |> order_by([e], desc: e.inserted_at)
    |> preload(:actor)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp filter_by_subject(query, subject_id),
    do: where(query, [e], e.subject_id == ^subject_id)

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, blank) when blank in [nil, ""], do: query

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, %Date{} = date),
    do: where(query, [e], e.inserted_at >= ^start_of_day(date))

  defp filter_by_date_from(query, date_string) when is_binary(date_string),

    do: filter_by_date_to(query, Date.from_iso8601!(date_string))

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

defmodule Mix.Tasks.Spex do
  @shortdoc "Run executable specifications (spex)"
  @moduledoc """
  Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

  SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
  both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.

  Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
  - setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  - setup: State reset between tests
  - Context passing between test steps
  - Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

  ## Usage

      mix spex                    # Run all spex files
      mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
      mix spex --help             # Show this help

  ## Options

      --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
      --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
      --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
      --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
      --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
      --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
      --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
      --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
                      Can be specified multiple times
      --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
      --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
      --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)

  ## Examples

      mix spex
      mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
      mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
      mix spex --verbose
      mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
      mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
      mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
      mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
      mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
      mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests

  ## Configuration

  You can configure spex behavior in your config files:

      config :sexy_spex,
        manual_mode: false,
        step_delay: 0

  Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all blocks.

  ## Important: Test Environment Setup

  To ensure spex runs in the test environment with proper module compilation,
  add this to your project's mix.exs:

      def project do
        [
          # ... other config
          preferred_cli_env: [
            spex: :test
          ]
        ]
      end

  This ensures that `mix spex` always runs in the test environment and compiles
  modules with test-specific code paths (e.g., test/support directories).

  """

  use Mix.Task

  alias Mix.Compilers.Test, as: CT

  @default_pattern "test/spex/**/*_spex.exs"
  @default_timeout 60_000

  def run(args) do
    # Ensure we're running in test environment for spex
    # Note: This task should have preferred_cli_env set to :test in mix.exs
    # of projects using spex to ensure proper compilation

    # Compile the project to ensure test environment modules are loaded
    Mix.Task.run("compile")

    # Start the application like mix test does
    # This ensures all applications and their dependencies are started
    Mix.Task.run("app.start")

    # Pre-process args to handle --jsonl without value (convert to --jsonl=default)
    args = preprocess_jsonl_arg(args)

    {opts, files, _} = OptionParser.parse(args,
      switches: [
        only_spex: :boolean,
        pattern: :string,
        verbose: :boolean,
        timeout: :integer,
        help: :boolean,
        manual: :boolean,
        speed: :string,
        trace: :boolean,
        slowest: :integer,
        formatter: :keep,
        jsonl: :string,
        stale: :boolean,
        force: :boolean
      ],
      aliases: [
        h: :help,
        v: :verbose,
        m: :manual,
        s: :speed,
        t: :trace,
        f: :formatter,
        j: :jsonl
      ]
    )

    if opts[:help] do
      Mix.shell().info(@moduledoc)
      return()
    end

    # Find spex files
    spex_files = find_spex_files(files, opts)

    if Enum.empty?(spex_files) do
      pattern = opts[:pattern] || @default_pattern
      Mix.shell().info("No spex files found matching pattern: #{pattern}")
      Mix.shell().info("Try: mix spex --help")
      # Exit early if no files found
      System.halt(0)
    end

    # Configure spex execution
    configure_spex_mode(opts)

    if opts[:verbose] do
      Mix.shell().info("Running #{length(spex_files)} spex file(s)...")
    end

    # Run spex tests with ExUnit
    run_tests_with_exunit(spex_files, opts)
  end

  defp return, do: :ok

  # Handle --jsonl without a value: if the next arg looks like a file, don't consume it
  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(args) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(args, [])
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg([], acc), do: Enum.reverse(acc)

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(["--jsonl" | rest], acc) do
    case rest do
      [next | remaining] when is_binary(next) ->
        # If next arg starts with - or ends with .exs, treat --jsonl as having default value
        if String.starts_with?(next, "-") or String.ends_with?(next, ".exs") do
          preprocess_jsonl_arg(rest, ["--jsonl=spex_failures.jsonl" | acc])
        else
          # Next arg is the jsonl path, skip it
          preprocess_jsonl_arg(remaining, ["--jsonl=#{next}" | acc])
        end
      [] ->
        # --jsonl at end with no value
        Enum.reverse(["--jsonl=spex_failures.jsonl" | acc])
    end
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(["-j" | rest], acc) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(["--jsonl" | rest], acc)
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg([arg | rest], acc) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(rest, [arg | acc])
  end

  defp find_spex_files([], opts) do
    # No specific files provided, use pattern
    pattern = opts[:pattern] || @default_pattern
    Path.wildcard(pattern)
  end

  defp find_spex_files(files, _opts) do
    # Specific files provided
    Enum.filter(files, &File.exists?/1)
  end

  defp configure_spex_mode(opts) do
    # Quiet by default; verbose opts in
    unless opts[:verbose] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :quiet, true)
    end

    # Configure JSONL output if requested
    if opts[:jsonl] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :jsonl_enabled, true)
      path = if is_binary(opts[:jsonl]) and opts[:jsonl] != "true",
        do: opts[:jsonl],
        else: "spex_failures.jsonl"
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :jsonl_path, path)
      # Clear file at start
      File.write!(path, "")
    end

    # Set manual mode if requested
    if opts[:manual] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :manual_mode, true)
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 0)
      if opts[:verbose], do: Mix.shell().info("Manual mode enabled - you'll be prompted at each step")
    else
      # Configure speed if provided
      configure_speed(opts[:speed], opts[:verbose])
    end
  end

  defp configure_speed(nil, verbose), do: configure_speed("fast", verbose)
  defp configure_speed("fast", _verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 0)
  end
  defp configure_speed("medium", verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 1000)
    if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("Medium speed mode - 1s delays between steps")
  end
  defp configure_speed("slow", verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 2500)
    if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("Slow speed mode - 2.5s delays between steps")
  end
  defp configure_speed(invalid, _verbose) do
    Mix.shell().error("Invalid speed: #{invalid}. Valid options: fast, medium, slow")
    System.halt(1)
  end

  defp parse_formatters(opts) do
    formatters =
      opts
      |> Keyword.get_values(:formatter)
      |> Enum.map(&parse_formatter_module/1)

    if Enum.empty?(formatters) do
      [ExUnit.CLIFormatter]
    else
      formatters
    end
  end

  defp parse_formatter_module(name) do
    module = Module.concat([name])

    unless Code.ensure_loaded?(module) do
      Mix.shell().error("Could not load formatter module: #{name}")
      System.halt(1)
    end

    module
  end

  defp run_tests_with_exunit(spex_files, opts) do
    if opts[:stale] do
      run_with_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts)
    else
      run_without_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts)
    end
  end

  defp run_without_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts) do
    opts
    |> build_exunit_config()
    |> ExUnit.start()

    load_spex_files(spex_files, opts)

    ExUnit.run()
    |> handle_results()
  end

  defp run_with_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts) do
    exunit_config = build_exunit_config(opts)
    ExUnit.start(exunit_config)

    test_paths = spex_test_paths()
    test_elixirc_options = Mix.Project.config()[:test_elixirc_options] || []

    case CT.require_and_run(spex_files, test_paths, test_elixirc_options, opts) do
      {:ok, results} ->
        handle_results(results)

      :noop ->
        if opts[:verbose] do
          Mix.shell().info("No stale spex files")
        end

        System.halt(0)
    end
  end

  defp spex_test_paths do
    # Return the directory containing spex files so the stale manifest
    # can find test_helper.exs (falls back gracefully if not present)
    ["test/spex"]
  end

  defp build_exunit_config(opts) do
    timeout = opts[:timeout] || @default_timeout
    formatters = parse_formatters(opts)

    config = [
      colors: [enabled: true],
      formatters: formatters,
      timeout: timeout
    ]

    config
    |> maybe_enable_trace(opts[:verbose])
    |> maybe_enable_trace(opts[:trace])
    |> maybe_set_slowest(opts[:slowest])
  end

  defp maybe_enable_trace(config, true), do: Keyword.put(config, :trace, true)
  defp maybe_enable_trace(config, _), do: config

  defp maybe_set_slowest(config, n) when is_integer(n) and n > 0,
    do: Keyword.put(config, :slowest, n)

  defp maybe_set_slowest(config, _), do: config

  # When the :spex compiler (from client_utils) already compiled these files,
  # suppress "redefining module" warnings — we still need Code.require_file
  # so modules register with ExUnit.
  defp load_spex_files(spex_files, _opts) do
    already_compiled = spex_already_compiled?()
    if already_compiled, do: Code.put_compiler_option(:ignore_module_conflict, true)

    Enum.each(spex_files, fn file ->
      try do
        Code.require_file(file)
      rescue
        error ->
          Mix.shell().error("Failed to load #{file}: #{Exception.message(error)}")
          System.halt(1)
      end
    end)

    if already_compiled, do: Code.put_compiler_option(:ignore_module_conflict, false)
  end

  defp spex_already_compiled? do
    :persistent_term.get({Mix.Tasks.Compile.Spex, :diagnostics}, nil) != nil
  end

  defp handle_results(result) do
    verbose = !Application.get_env(:sexy_spex, :quiet, true)

    case result do
      %{failures: 0} ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("All spex passed!")
        System.halt(0)

      %{failures: failures} when failures > 0 ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().error("#{failures} spex failed")
        System.halt(1)

      _ ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().error("Spex execution encountered errors")
        System.halt(1)
    end
  end

end

    end

    # Find spex files
    spex_files = find_spex_files(files, opts)

    if Enum.empty?(spex_files) do
      pattern = opts[:pattern] || @default_pattern
      Mix.shell().info("No spex files found matching pattern: #{pattern}")
      Mix.shell().info("Try: mix spex --help")
      # Exit early if no files found
      System.halt(0)
    end

    # Configure spex execution
    configure_spex_mode(opts)

    if opts[:verbose] do
      Mix.shell().info("Running #{length(spex_files)} spex file(s)...")
    end

    # Run spex tests with ExUnit
    run_tests_with_exunit(spex_files, opts)
  end

  defp return, do: :ok

  # Handle --jsonl without a value: if the next arg looks like a file, don't consume it
  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(args) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(args, [])
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg([], acc), do: Enum.reverse(acc)

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(["--jsonl" | rest], acc) do
    case rest do
      [next | remaining] when is_binary(next) ->
        # If next arg starts with - or ends with .exs, treat --jsonl as having default value
        if String.starts_with?(next, "-") or String.ends_with?(next, ".exs") do
          preprocess_jsonl_arg(rest, ["--jsonl=spex_failures.jsonl" | acc])
        else
          # Next arg is the jsonl path, skip it
          preprocess_jsonl_arg(remaining, ["--jsonl=#{next}" | acc])
        end
      [] ->
        # --jsonl at end with no value
        Enum.reverse(["--jsonl=spex_failures.jsonl" | acc])
    end
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg(["-j" | rest], acc) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(["--jsonl" | rest], acc)
  end

  defp preprocess_jsonl_arg([arg | rest], acc) do
    preprocess_jsonl_arg(rest, [arg | acc])
  end

  defp find_spex_files([], opts) do
    # No specific files provided, use pattern
    pattern = opts[:pattern] || @default_pattern
    Path.wildcard(pattern)
  end

  defp find_spex_files(files, _opts) do
    # Specific files provided
    Enum.filter(files, &File.exists?/1)
  end

  defp configure_spex_mode(opts) do
    # Quiet by default; verbose opts in
    unless opts[:verbose] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :quiet, true)
    end

    # Configure JSONL output if requested
    if opts[:jsonl] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :jsonl_enabled, true)
      path = if is_binary(opts[:jsonl]) and opts[:jsonl] != "true",
        do: opts[:jsonl],
        else: "spex_failures.jsonl"
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :jsonl_path, path)
      # Clear file at start
      File.write!(path, "")
    end

    # Set manual mode if requested
    if opts[:manual] do
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :manual_mode, true)
      Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 0)
      if opts[:verbose], do: Mix.shell().info("Manual mode enabled - you'll be prompted at each step")
    else
      # Configure speed if provided
      configure_speed(opts[:speed], opts[:verbose])
    end
  end

  defp configure_speed(nil, verbose), do: configure_speed("fast", verbose)
  defp configure_speed("fast", _verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 0)
  end
  defp configure_speed("medium", verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 1000)
    if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("Medium speed mode - 1s delays between steps")
  end
  defp configure_speed("slow", verbose) do
    Application.put_env(:sexy_spex, :step_delay, 2500)
    if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("Slow speed mode - 2.5s delays between steps")
  end
  defp configure_speed(invalid, _verbose) do
    Mix.shell().error("Invalid speed: #{invalid}. Valid options: fast, medium, slow")
    System.halt(1)
  end

  defp parse_formatters(opts) do
    formatters =
      opts
      |> Keyword.get_values(:formatter)
      |> Enum.map(&parse_formatter_module/1)

    if Enum.empty?(formatters) do
      [ExUnit.CLIFormatter]
    else
      formatters
    end
  end

  defp parse_formatter_module(name) do
    module = Module.concat([name])

    unless Code.ensure_loaded?(module) do
      Mix.shell().error("Could not load formatter module: #{name}")
      System.halt(1)
    end

    module
  end

  defp run_tests_with_exunit(spex_files, opts) do
    if opts[:stale] do
      run_with_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts)
    else
      run_without_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts)
    end
  end

  defp run_without_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts) do
    opts
    |> build_exunit_config()
    |> ExUnit.start()

    load_spex_files(spex_files, opts)

    ExUnit.run()
    |> handle_results()
  end

  defp run_with_stale_tracking(spex_files, opts) do
    exunit_config = build_exunit_config(opts)
    ExUnit.start(exunit_config)

    test_paths = spex_test_paths()
    test_elixirc_options = Mix.Project.config()[:test_elixirc_options] || []

    case CT.require_and_run(spex_files, test_paths, test_elixirc_options, opts) do
      {:ok, results} ->
        handle_results(results)

      :noop ->
        if opts[:verbose] do
          Mix.shell().info("No stale spex files")
        end

        System.halt(0)
    end
  end

  defp spex_test_paths do
    # Return the directory containing spex files so the stale manifest
    # can find test_helper.exs (falls back gracefully if not present)
    ["test/spex"]
  end

  defp build_exunit_config(opts) do
    timeout = opts[:timeout] || @default_timeout
    formatters = parse_formatters(opts)

    config = [
      colors: [enabled: true],
      formatters: formatters,
      timeout: timeout
    ]

    config
    |> maybe_enable_trace(opts[:verbose])
    |> maybe_enable_trace(opts[:trace])
    |> maybe_set_slowest(opts[:slowest])
  end

  defp maybe_enable_trace(config, true), do: Keyword.put(config, :trace, true)
  defp maybe_enable_trace(config, _), do: config

  defp maybe_set_slowest(config, n) when is_integer(n) and n > 0,
    do: Keyword.put(config, :slowest, n)

  defp maybe_set_slowest(config, _), do: config

  # When the :spex compiler (from client_utils) already compiled these files,
  # suppress "redefining module" warnings — we still need Code.require_file
  # so modules register with ExUnit.
  defp load_spex_files(spex_files, _opts) do
    already_compiled = spex_already_compiled?()
    if already_compiled, do: Code.put_compiler_option(:ignore_module_conflict, true)

    Enum.each(spex_files, fn file ->
      try do
        Code.require_file(file)
      rescue
        error ->
          Mix.shell().error("Failed to load #{file}: #{Exception.message(error)}")
          System.halt(1)
      end
    end)

    if already_compiled, do: Code.put_compiler_option(:ignore_module_conflict, false)
  end

  defp spex_already_compiled? do
    :persistent_term.get({Mix.Tasks.Compile.Spex, :diagnostics}, nil) != nil
  end

  defp handle_results(result) do
    verbose = !Application.get_env(:sexy_spex, :quiet, true)

    case result do
      %{failures: 0} ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().info("All spex passed!")
        System.halt(0)

      %{failures: failures} when failures > 0 ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().error("#{failures} spex failed")
        System.halt(1)

      _ ->
        if verbose, do: Mix.shell().error("Spex execution encountered errors")
        System.halt(1)
    end
  end

end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7107Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7107 — Adding a property under an existing client saves it
  and lists it under that client as its only owning client.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "owner adds a property to an existing client" do
    scenario "the property is saved and listed under its client" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client \"Sarah Kim\" exists", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Sarah Kim")
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_path, client_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner adds a property \"123 Oak St\" and assigns it to Sarah Kim", context do
        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, context.client_path, %{service_address: "123 Oak St"})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :property_path, property_path)}
      end

      then_ "the property is saved and listed under Sarah Kim", context do
        {:ok, _client_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.client_path)
        assert html =~ "123 Oak St"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the property shows Sarah Kim as its only owning client", context do
        {:ok, property_live, html} = live(context.conn, context.property_path)

        assert has_element?(property_live, "[data-test='property-client']", "Sarah Kim")
        assert length(Regex.scan(~r/data-test="property-client"/, html)) == 1

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  def add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(%{user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id, role: role})
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        case member.role do
          :owner ->
            owner_count = count_owners(account_id)
            if owner_count > 1, do: Repo.delete(member), else: {:error, :last_owner}

          _ ->
            Repo.delete(member)
        end
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_found}

      member ->
        changeset = Member.update_role_changeset(member, %{role: role})
        validated_changeset = Member.validate_owner_exists(changeset, Repo)

        case validated_changeset.valid? do
          true -> Repo.update(validated_changeset)
          false -> {:error, validated_changeset}
        end
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(user_id, account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Member, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> nil
      member -> member.role
    end
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(user_id, account_id) do
    Repo.exists?(from m in Member, where: m.user_id == ^user_id and m.account_id == ^account_id)
  end

  def can_add_user_to_account?(_account_id), do: true

  def count_account_users(account_id) do
    Repo.aggregate(from(m in Member, where: m.account_id == ^account_id), :count)
  end

  def list_user_accounts(user_id) do
    from(a in Account,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.account_id == a.id,
      where: m.user_id == ^user_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def list_account_users(account_id) do
    from(u in User,
      join: m in Member,
      on: m.user_id == u.id,
      where: m.account_id == ^account_id
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end
